picks.what: View from the Tagus, lithograph (British Museum)
picks.why: post-earthquake riverfront with the castle above; only post-1755 general view

picks.what: The Rossio, the Baixa and the castle hill, photograph

gaps: P0: no candidates. No 1755 earthquake or ruins view among the candidates.
notes: #11 (1694) is a reduced copy of Braun and Hogenberg’s 1598 bird’s-eye plan, so it shows the city of the 1590s; kept as the only P2 option of quality (#14, a 1726 river view, is small and also a copy). #19’s date is the British Museum’s range (lithography era); it shows the rebuilt post-earthquake riverfront, castle and cathedral towers. #17 (an English view of pre-earthquake Lisbon) skipped: date only ‘18th century’. #28 is the Rue de Lisbonne in Paris and #29 is Lisbon, Ohio; #31 shows the Ajuda palace, not São Vicente. P4 1895 panorama photos (#23, #24) are too narrow and only 39 years after 1856.
